reviews.text: There is also plenty to unpack in the film's various narrative threads, from the fascinating investigative trail that the searchers follow, chasing down record label owners, producers, and Detroit barflies, to the story's exotically pre-digital flavour...
reviews.author: Michael Leader

reviews.text: The driving force of Searching For Sugar Man is the fans, and their journey from the discovery of their favourite singer to the sell-out South African shows he plays 30 years after...
reviews.author: Rebecca Schiller

reviews.text: If you go see Searching for Sugar Man - and I suggest you do - try not to know too much about him beforehand.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Stranger than fiction, this is an incredible story about a true talent.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: Benefits from camera work by Camilla Skagerstrom that is nothing short of amazing and beautiful and the perfect meditative counterpart to Rodriguez's music.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: Although its attempts to play out as some sort of missing person drama perhaps sit at odds with its subject, the film is an engrossing yarn with a touch of visual flair from Malik Bendjelloul.
reviews.author: Jim Ross

reviews.text: Searching for Sugar Man is a sensitive yet creative documentary. Great for music and film fans alike.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: By far the best aspect of the film is to discover the music of Rodriguez, whose haunting lyrics truly were never appreciated in his native country.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: A heart-warming documentary about holding onto your dreams -- and perhaps one of this year's most enjoyable and accomplished films.
reviews.author: Patrick Gamble

reviews.text: It is the model of the modern music documentary, which shines a well-deserved light on obscure artists or periods of their lives, and presents it in a way that appeals to broader audiences than mere music obsessives.
reviews.author: Benjamin H. Smith

reviews.text: The best, most touching, most humbling documentary I've ever seen about a musician I've never heard of.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: Whether or not you know what finally happened to the film's subject, the reality is as rewarding as the myth.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: It becomes a portrait of a man who outlasted his times and went on to live in peace...
reviews.author: Steve Erickson

reviews.text: Director Malik Bendjelloul attempts clear the air and really analyze the thoughts and emotions that formed Sixto Rodriguez's past work.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: An emotional fairy tale that doesn't fall into the melodramatic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rafael Paz

reviews.text: A first-rate doc about the unsung Latino Bob Dylan who almost single-handedly brought the spirit of American civil rights protests to South Africa's fight against apartheid through his music.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: So lightweight and underdeveloped, you leave the theatre feeling like they still haven't found him yet.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Intriguing docu about missing musician; some language, pot.
reviews.author: S. Jhoanna Robledo

reviews.text: As a documentary, "Searching for Sugar Man" falls short, but as an enormously satisfying feel-good story it hits the mark.
reviews.author: James Plath

reviews.text: You can still enjoy the film. I did, but it's nothing more than a fairy tale.
reviews.author: Mark Aitken

reviews.text: [Rodriguez] is a highly unusual and fascinating human being, and Searching for Sugar Man is a very interesting look at his life, his music, and the strange, fickle nature of fame.
reviews.author: Ezra Stead

reviews.text: There's no arguing this is a remarkable story, and director Malik Bendjelloul tells it beautifully, creating a powerful sense of mystery and discovery even when we're tipped off to how the story ends.
reviews.author: Mark Deming

reviews.text: At 85 minutes, it's a tight, sharp achievement, yet one of the things I love about it is simple: It moves to a relaxed rhythm, in sync with its slightly otherworldly subject.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: A nimble and engaging documentary, less about a man than about a myth -- and about the experience of loving an under-loved artist.
reviews.author: Jon Frosch

reviews.text: 'Searching For Sugar Man' simply shouts out for celebration!
reviews.author: Jennifer Merin

reviews.text: "Searching for Sugar Man" is a valentine to every artist who feels like he toils away in obscurity, unsure of or unaware of the impact he might make on the world.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Fortunately filmmaker Bendjelloul decided that Rodriguez's story needed to be told - one of the most fascinating biographies ever put on film.
reviews.author: Bruce Bennett

reviews.text: Part music documentary, part mystery, all inspirational homage to unrecognized genius everywhere.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: For the most part an endearing documentary about mystery Bob Dylan-like singer Sixto Rodriguez.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: An amazing story. If music is the glue of the world then Rodriguez is the super glue.
reviews.author: Cameron Williams

reviews.text: Does a nice job of presenting the mystery and history of Rodriguez... but seems incomplete, and biased in favor of its predetermined narrative.
reviews.author: John Beifuss

reviews.text: Rodriguez, once he emerges from the mists, appears to be a sweet, decent - and remarkably intact - soul. One wonders if he had achieved his rock 'n' roll dreams, would his daughters have turned out so well?
reviews.author: Philip Martin

reviews.text: There's a fascinating story in the rise and fall of singer-songwriter Sixto Rodriguez, "the Latin Bob Dylan," and it's too bad that the documentary "Searching for Sugar Man" doesn't tell enough of it.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A soulful, lip-tremblingly joyous movie that's one of the more affecting experiences I've had in a cinema this year.
reviews.author: Aaron Yap

reviews.text: Engrossing even when it's a little unfocused.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: One of the most bizarre pop music documentaries ever...a singularly fascinating true-life tale that many of its participants still find difficult to believe.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: ...it isn't merely the content that makes Searching for Sugar Man so affecting: it's the way that Swedish filmmaker Malik Bendjelloul sets up the story and peels away the mystery of Rodriguez, one layer at time.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: A mystery as compelling as any fictional detective story.
reviews.author: Duane Dudek

reviews.text: The first half of this film is mysterious whereas the second half is wonderfully inspiring. It's proof that truth really is stranger than fiction.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: This is a fine documentary; insightful and entertaining with a genteel approach to uncovering a figure so close to the hearts of an unexpected fan base.
reviews.author: Patrick Kolan

reviews.text: A celebration of an artist and the power of art to transcend time and place
reviews.author: Thomas Caldwell

reviews.text: Much credit to director Malik Bendjelloul for surprising this cynical and desensitised film watcher.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: For those familiar with the story of Rodriguez, this engaging documentary on his substantial success in South Africa will prove both illuminating and bemusing.
reviews.author: Ed Gibbs

reviews.text: I was instantly hooked by this unique documentary...If you are a traveller on the road of life, don't miss this unforgettable treasure of a film
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: This is not only the best documentary I've seen this year, it's one that shows other documentaries how to do it.
reviews.author: Ken Hanke

reviews.text: Searching for Sugar Man reminds us that a wise man knows lasting riches are never the result of record sales.
reviews.author: Lawrence Toppman

reviews.text: Searching for Sugar Man" is a saga about the power of music, living life on one's own terms and the joy of second chances.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: The search for a long-lost pop icon has an unexpected payoff.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: [A] moving, lyrical account ...
reviews.author: Ken Marks

reviews.text: Two fans, Stephen Segerman and Craig Bertholomew, made it their business to find out exactly what happened to the singer Rodriguez. And, "Searching for Sugar Man" is the fruits of their labor. The fruit is tasting pretty sweet.
reviews.author: Paul Chambers

reviews.text: It starts as a bittersweet parable about the cruelty of commerce, but the wonder of "Searching for Sugar Man" will not soon slip away.
reviews.author: Joe Williams

reviews.text: Director Malik Bendjelloul's engaging, cleverly structured documentary about the legendary folk singer Rodriguez is shaped like a mystery.
reviews.author: Rene Rodriguez

reviews.text: You watch "Searching for Sugar Man" at first fascinated by the mystery - what happened to Rodriguez? Where did he go? Then you become infuriated by its revelations of financial injustice.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: If you like music, a good mystery or, better yet, a combination of both, you won't be disappointed.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: An unexpectedly fresh nonfiction tale that rustles up deep feelings of a life stolen -- part docu-mystery, part uplifting valentine about the universality and resonating power of music.
reviews.author: Brent Simon

reviews.text: Generates immediate interest in a forgotten artist, permitting the delicate yet barbed tunes to guide the experience, returning a sense of excitement to a man who unfortunately missed out on the highlights of his career.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: It isn't that Searching for Sugar Man's plot developments are gotcha!-like, but this documentary does boast some bowl-you-over reveals best experienced blind.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: Ultimately, for Rodriguez, musical redemption transcends the greed and soul-sapping breaks he encountered.
reviews.author: George Varga

reviews.text: Rodriguez's life story is only part of what makes "Searching for Sugar Man" such a revelation.
reviews.author: Marc Mohan

reviews.text: The man and his music are worth checking out, even if the movie is not.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Ultimately an ode to Rodriguez's artistic modesty and the power of his music-a rousing crowd-pleaser that asks you to save questions for another film.
reviews.author: Ben Kenigsberg

reviews.text: Submitted for your approval: one Sixto Rodriguez, a Mexican-American singer/songwriter whom Rod Serling would surely embrace, in or out of the Twilight Zone.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: A rousing and all-encompassing look at a man who becomes even more of a mystery after we've gotten to know him.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Beautiful and revelatory, Searching for Sugar Man also incorporates huge chunks of Rodriguez's music.
reviews.author: Steven Rea

reviews.text: A rock documentary that goes way behind the music to tell a story that seems pure urban legend.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Here's the rare music documentary in which the narrative is more interesting than the songs.
reviews.author: Ben Sachs

reviews.text: An inspirational, spiritual experience which illustrates how the purity of soul required to produce the finest works is not dependent on material gain.
reviews.author: Graham Young

reviews.text: Bendjelloul mixes modern footage of Detroit with archival and animated images, and the shots of Rodriguez marching through his home turf help viewers understand what makes him tick.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Fascinating music doc makes you believe the unbelievable.
reviews.author: Matt Pais

reviews.text: Through a mix of standard talking-head interviews, animated sequences, and archival footage, Bendjelloul unlocks a mystery, painting a compelling portrait of a hidden rock icon.
reviews.author: Brett Michel

reviews.text: I hope you're able to see this film. You deserve to. And yes, it exists because we need for it to.
reviews.author: Roger Ebert

reviews.text: This is a real-life fairy tale with a remarkably happy ending.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: A pleasing fix, Searching for Sugar Man is a lost-and-found film about pursuits - one of them abandoned, and one not.
reviews.author: Brad Wheeler

reviews.text: The movie is neatly structured, and Rodriguez turns out to be an interesting guy. He's worth getting to know, even if his music isn't.
reviews.author: Mark Jenkins

reviews.text: Music executive Clarence Avant says Rodriguez sold about six copies of each of his two albums. Multiply that by the number of people who see this movie.
reviews.author: Peter Hartlaub

reviews.text: Through interviews and animations, this entertaining musical mystery tour. . .traces. . .an engaging story so full of colorful characters . . .that I was leery of a hoax.
reviews.author: Nora Lee Mandel

reviews.text: It may fiddle with the facts, but this documentary on the hunt for a long-lost 70s music legend offers a brilliant insight into the nature of fame.
reviews.author: Philip French

reviews.text: Search out this fine, fascinating, warmhearted documentary.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: If it were a fiction, you wouldn't believe it at all.
reviews.author: Derek Malcolm

reviews.text: Sugar Man is most interesting when it touches on the conditions that combined to draw a cult hero out of some decent music and a generously enabled, imagination-firing mystique.
reviews.author: Michelle Orange

reviews.text: Hopefully, it will have the benefit of giving a second chance to the music of Rodriguez, which would be fitting given his story.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: A fantastic music doc with a surprising twist; which, when done as well as it is here, works just as effectively whether you know what's coming or not.
reviews.author: Ian Buckwalter

reviews.text: Imagine the story of Nick Drake with a happy ending and you will have some idea what to expect from this terrific, staggeringly unlikely documentary.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Archive footage is seamlessly interwoven with interviews, building to a glorious final flourish that makes your heart sing.
A fascinating look at a "lost" musician from the late '60s as well as a meditation on the confluence of fame, art and riches.
reviews.author: Kimberly Gadette

reviews.text: Singer-songwriter Rodriguez was supposed to have been the next Bob Dylan. What happened? Swedish documentary maker Malik Bendjelloul's stirring, surprising and deeply touching film has the answer.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: A terrific documentary about a decades-long search, by two South African Rodriguez fans, for the story behind their enigmatic pop idol.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: The rustic folk-rock sound and politically provocative lyrics provide the seductive soundtrack for the film. They often serve as a stand-in for the artist as well. It is how we get to know him.
reviews.author: Betsy Sharkey

reviews.text: Certain details about Rodriguez, especially his personal life, remain in shadow, calling into question whether they would have interfered with the inspirational narrative.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: This film tells a tale far too incredible to be true - yet it is, indeed, a documentary.
reviews.author: Christopher Tookey

reviews.text: My real hope is that, yes, the movie does well, but that rereleases by Light in the Attic Records of the music will establish Rodriguez as an artist in the U.S.
reviews.author: Kirk Honeycutt

reviews.text: The way in which this fascinating story unfolds, as directed by Swedish filmmaker Malik Bendjelloul, renders it thoroughly captivating, often exhilarating.
reviews.author: Claudia Puig

reviews.text: A hugely appealing documentary about fans, faith and an enigmatic Age of Aquarius musician who burned bright and hopeful before disappearing.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Searching for Sugar Man is a fresh and unexpected documentary that plays like a nail-biting mystery and a ticket to ride the whirlwind where art and commerce do battle.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: Listen, be moved, and pass it on.
reviews.author: Elizabeth Weitzman

reviews.text: Well, director Malik Bendjelloul's title is a bit misleading, but he knew a great story when he heard one.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The movie's most potent emotional payoff is less Rodriguez's delayed success story - the fulfillment of many a frustrated rocker's fantasies - than the mysteries it leaves unsolved.
reviews.author: Ella Taylor

reviews.text: An inspiring and uplifting documentary about a man who gives all he's got and experiences a miracle in return.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: The lilting, honeyed soundtrack, made up of Rodriguez's own songs, makes his relative obscurity here seem all the more puzzling.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: It's the triumph of this documentary that we feel, after learning so much about a game-changed yet weirdly unchangeable street messiah, who we're told still lives in his demi-hovel, that there is more to learn yet.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: I can't remember the last time a film rocked my world and blew my mind like... [t]his is a wholly extraordinary movie [does]...
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Poignant, touching and inspiring, even if it doesn't tell you quite as much as you'd like to know about Sixto Rodriquez, to give him his full name.
reviews.author: Henry Fitzherbert

reviews.text: The truth about him - hard to get at in that pre-internet age, and still not entirely illuminated in this film - turned out to be stranger than fiction.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: An absorbing and uplifting doc that rivals Catfish for sheer stranger-than-fiction thrills. Great soundtrack, too.
reviews.author: Adam Woodward

reviews.text: We're fed plenty of sugar in this authorized fairy tale, but are left hungry for beef.
reviews.author: Lisa Schwarzbaum

reviews.text: Hugely entertaining and powerfully emotional, this is a terrific, well made documentary that tells a gripping story and unearths an astonishing musical find; it's also one of the best films of the year.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: This innovative documentary tells a stranger-than-fiction tale about a remarkable Phil Ochs-like singer/songwriter from the Motor City who metaphorically rises from the dead, to the delight of his South African fans and now us.
reviews.author: Wendy Weinstein

reviews.text: Fluid, open-ended documentaries that demand more of an audience than foregone assent or fleeting bouts of passive outrage are rare these days, which is what makes Malik Bendjelloul's Searching for Sugar Man such a gift.
reviews.author: Mark Holcomb

reviews.text: A diverting but frustrating quasiprofile, one that doesn't have the answers to its own questions.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: All you really have to know about this surprising and emotive music doc is that you should see it.
reviews.author: Trevor Johnston

reviews.text: A gloriously inspirational comeback tale that leaves you feeling anything is possible.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: A remarkable tribute to uncompromising talent and fiercely devoted fandom.
reviews.author: Siobhan Synnot

reviews.text: Music fans will love this indie documentary. Try to avoid Googling him before you watch, though.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: Unlike most nonfiction films, which tend to focus on uncovering misdeed and outrage, this one leaves you joyous and moved..You'll come away with a lump in your throat.
reviews.author: Marshall Fine

reviews.text: A story as heart-warming as it is genuine, as the humble Rodriguez gets his long overdue recognition on a triumphant return to South Africa.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The tale is better than the telling - and the soundtrack's better still - but music this monumental demands its moment. Now go and buy the album.
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: [VIDEO ESSAY] Spoiler alert: "Searching for Sugar Man" is a truly inspiring and thoroughly entertaining documentary.
reviews.author: Cole Smithey

reviews.text: Despite crafting a consistently engaging film, the director doesn't present the full scope of Sixto Rodriguez's life.
reviews.author: Chris Cabin

reviews.text: He just plays his songs and counts his blessings, and it is a pleasure to spend the 90 minutes of this warm, kind film with him.
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: A documentary about fandom and freedom, information and misinformation, fleeting fame and everlasting art, it tackles all of these qualities with remarkable ease and - of course - a great soundtrack.
reviews.author: William Goss

reviews.text: The narrative, as it is so dependent on vague and redundant talking heads, is disappointingly shallow and trivial ... thanks to the producers the storytelling is engaging.
reviews.author: Christopher Campbell

reviews.text: Could easily be a breakout documentary-one that might also invigorate the impressive back catalogue of a deserving and relatively unknown musical artist.
reviews.author: Ray Greene

reviews.text: Though manipulative in its storytelling and structure, Searching For Sugar Man ultimately earns its happy ending by alchemizing pain into transcendent beauty.
reviews.author: Nathan Rabin

reviews.text: I'll praise the quality of director Malik Bendjelloul's storytelling, which is gripping from the opening shot almost to the last.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: Searching for Sugar Man is a winning musical detective story about a failed, forgotten early '70s rocker who became a huge success halfway across the world.
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: In a deft interplay of dogged investigation and randomness, Bendjelloul shows how facts surface to dispel a persistent myth that Rodriguez shot himself on stage.
reviews.author: David D'Arcy

reviews.text: A born crowd-pleaser whose central mystery begets a great triumph of grace and modesty.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: While all the interview subjects are enthusiastic, the overall lack of familiarity with Rodriquez's personal background and career collapse begin to drag.
reviews.author: Justin Lowe

synopsis: Though he faded into obscurity in the U.S., an early '70s musician known as Rodriguez became a huge hit in South Africa and was widely rumored to have died. Two obsessed fans set out to learn the man's true fate.
